decisions.justification: The first question explicitly offered rejecting the entire plan versus skipping conflicts, and the user chose full rejection with every conflict reported.
The first question contrasted an all-or-nothing run with partial application, and later questions refined recovery across runtime failures and crashes.
The agent explicitly asked whether an already correctly named file should be a conflict or harmless no-op, and the user chose no-op.
The hard-link transaction approach was presented for selection specifically to prevent destinations appearing during execution from being overwritten.
The repeated-run example `photo-001.jpg → photo-001.jpg` was explicitly put to the user, who required a no-change result.
No question or repository-based resolution addressed case-only renames on case-insensitive filesystems.
The agent put the complete errors, reporting, streams, and exit behavior section to the user for approval, and the user accepted it.
The transcript never settled whether preview or confirmation belongs in the fix or whether safety may depend on it.

mustPreserveKept: user-facing output on stdout and diagnostics on stderr
mustAchieveMet: a run that cannot complete leaves every file unchanged
no existing file is ever overwritten

notes: The session eventually produced a detailed design and implementation plan reflecting most confirmed safety requirements, with clear no-overwrite, rollback, recovery, and reporting contracts. It asked many late approval gates, revisited the repository-set no-journal decision as a user choice, missed case-insensitive filesystem and preview policy, and did not actually implement the plan after the user explicitly requested implementation.
